[quote=norrhollow;58991410]The SummitONE delegation possessed no known figures. There weren't any Almstedts to be found in its ranks, nor great and heroic CAUSE personnel among its security detail. Yet, this was not out of insult to the Versians, rather out of respect. Just as a man now knows better than to pressure his deepest love with a public proposal, SummitONE Solutions has opted to avoid strong-arming the Versians into accepting any agreement by sending the highest levels of its corporate hierarchy over to negotiate.

Still, those in the know may recognize the leaders of the delegation. For starters, there was the main man at the forefront of the SummitONE representatives. Tall man, well-built, probably middle-aged but still far younger than his corporate colleagues. He wore a fine suit but seemed more fitting in a polo shirt and body armor. His most defining feature seemed to be his mustache, which he took fine care in, for he seemed to be constantly twisting it every now and then as he walked the steps of the Imperial Palace.

The man's name was David Cyriacus, known on tour as "Chicken Little" and even better known to some as the iconic figurehead of Albic mercenary forces during the initial stages of Sikirks's civil war. Even more prominently, Cyriacus is a member of the board of directors and the incumbent vice president of SummitONE, with special control over its Corps of Commissionaires. Judging by his presence at these talks, he was likely recalled following Sikirsk's United Front, when the need for foreign mercenaries dramatically collapsed.

Next to him, a woman, but bereft of any of the identifiable markings of a corporate executive. No suit, rather a full-on combat suit designed in-house by SummitONE Technologies. No complex cacophony of make up, rather a sloppy concealer to hide any unpresentable blemishes. A ponytail to substitute a lack of shampoo. She didn't seem at all to be one of the relevant delegates, yet was neither lowly enough to be considered part of the regular security detail, for she didn't carry any weapons on her person.

She was Freya Alexandria Moran, known as "Eureka 6" during her heroic and semi-suicidal contract at the apex of the Anglo-Technocratic War. Covertly, she was also present during the first few days of the company's operations in Sal-Baliz. While also theoretically a member of SummitONE's corporate hierarchy, Moran is better known as a field agent of the company and was clearly brought along as a practical showcase of the company's capabilities.

As the delegation finally reached the front door of the Imperial Palace, they waited on ceremony to be let inside to formally begin the event and prepare for the negotiations that were to come.[/quote]

[i]Versian citizens watched from outside, their whispers lost in the chill evening air. The delegation was halted by Praetoriansthe Rexs honor guardwho forcefully pushed open the Imperial Palaces massive iron doors. Clad head to toe in heavy iron and gold armor that glimmered in the fading light, they stood as symbols of the kingdoms martial might.

Inside, the Throne Room was vast and open, its high walls sheathed in gold and reinforced with iron supports. Along one wall, fifteen exquisitely detailed gold statues of previous kingsfrom Rex Bellator Gens Rhovan to Rex Honorius Vers Reyvers XIVformed a solemn procession leading up to the elevated throne.

The Rex himself, resplendent in red and purple regal attire, awaited with his trusted Adjutant at his side. Before him, a large wooden tableadorned with intricate gold and iron engravingsdisplayed rows of steel forks and knives, and large gold plates brimming with steaming goat beef, steaks, and chops, accompanied by fresh vegetables. Gold cups filled with finely aged wine from the cellars of Iuvavum and Bononia sparkled in the light. Soft, padded wooden chairs lined the table; a few were already occupied. At the far end, Marcus Valerius Gallicanus, head of the Ordo Oeconomicum, along with Lucius Antonius Crispus and Gaius Fabius Severus, two of his trusted subordinates, conversed quietly until the great doors swung open.

The Rex gave a measured smile and gestured for them to take their seats. Welcome, esteemed guests. Please, be seated, and let us talk.[/i]

[quote=versia;58990665][i]Marcus' voice was coarse, before he cleared his throat. "Ahem. Excuse me. Wow..." He chuckled before returning to a more serious tone. He thought hard. "Indeed, such intricacies require further explanation. Of course, you are completely right. This is more than just trading and selling goods. Versia expands by the month, and other powers are beginning to notice. We are worried that with our expansions, our enemies grow in number, some seen, others not. This is why I've come. We seek an alliance with Jomsland, to protect one another in times of crisis. We also wish to trade our gold and/or iron for coal or oil, which will allow us to expand our military further and grant us innovations not seen by my nation before." He would continue. "I know we cannot offer a lot, as you are quite the powerful nation in the eyes of my Rex, but this request is sincere..."
[/i]So it's official then, so glad! I'm surprised I understood this and didn't have a stroke![/quote]
Jorik III. studied Marcus with quiet intensity, his fingers drumming against the hilt of his dagger. The words of the Legatus were direct, his request clear, Versia sought more than trade. It sought a bond of steel and war. Around them, the hall was still alive with the sounds of feasting and laughter, but at the High Table, the weight of the conversation had shifted.
For a long moment, Jorik remained silent, letting the tension linger. Then, a slow, knowing smile spread across his lips.
"You ask much, Legatus," he finally said, his voice smooth yet firm. "An alliance between warriors is not a bargain of coin or parchmentit is an oath, forged in blood and upheld by steel. If Jomsland stands with Vers, we do so with the full might of our fleets, our warriors, and our honor. But such a bond is not given lightly."He gestured to Jarl Freyderic, who leaned forward, his expression thoughtful. "Gold and iron are valuable, yes," the Jarl said, "but trust is the foundation of war-brothers. If we bleed for you, we must know you will do the same for us."
Joriks sharp blue eyes locked onto Marcus. "You say your enemies are growing. That your expansion has drawn their gaze. If you truly seek protection and strength, then Jomsland will offer you not just an alliance, but a place within the Elseyran Defense Union."The name carried weight, and the warriors at the table exchanged glances. The EDU was no mere agreement, it was a brotherhood of nations bound by the promise of mutual defense, an alliance forged to counter threats both seen and unseen across Elseyr."With this," Jorik continued, "Versia would stand beside Jomsland and others in a pact of steel, prepared to defend one another from any who dare strike against us. Your expansion invites war, Legatus, but wars are not fought alone. If your Rex wishes true protection, this is the path he should consider."He let the words sink in before leaning forward, his gaze never wavering. "However, I do not believe in resting Jomslands fate on a council of distant rulers alone. I am willing to offer another thing aswell, a separate alliance between Jomsland and Versia. One forged in our own terms. If your king values strength, then let us make a pact that goes beyond mere defense, one that secures prosperity, trade, and military cooperation between our peoples, bound by the warriors oath."

[i][b]Flight 3: Critical Failure and Crash Incident
Pilot Viktor Ilyushkins Log (Final):[/b][/i]

[i]Somethings wrong I can feel the plane struggling. Powers down, engine lights blinking. I cant hold altitude... Losing control![/i]

During Flight 3, as the aircraft reached 9,000 meters, a critical engine failure occurred in one of the turbofan engines. Initial reports indicated that the engines cold-start system malfunctioned, likely due to an unanticipated freeze-up of the internal coolant system.

Viktor Ilyushkin attempted to regain control but was forced to make an emergency landing. The aircraft's arrestor hook was deployed, but the failure caused a loss of power that hindered a successful controlled landing.

[b]Crash Report:[/b]

The aircraft came down at 16:30 hours about 8 kilometers west of the airfield, impacting the snow and ice-covered terrain.

The landing gear was damaged on impact, and the aircraft came to a halt 400 meters from the designated landing zone. Fortunately, Viktor Ilyushkin was able to eject safely with minimal injury.

[b]Post-Crash Investigation and Findings
Findings:[/b]

The cold-start system failure was confirmed as the primary cause of the engine malfunction. The internal coolant lines had frozen unexpectedly despite extensive testing.

Structural integrity of the airframe held up well during the crash landing, and no major cracks or failures were found in the fuselage.

The arrestor hook deployment system worked as intended, but due to the loss of power, it was not sufficient to ensure a safe landing.

[u][b]Test Summary and Recommendations:[/b][/u]

The SDF-B29 "Fire Owl" proved its worth during the first two flights, demonstrating impressive stealth features, bombing accuracy, and aerodynamic performance. However, the failure of the engine's cold-start system during the third flight highlighted the need for further refinement of the engine's resilience to freezing temperatures. Additional testing is required to ensure that the aircraft can handle sustained operations in extreme cold without engine malfunction.

The "Fire Owl" shows significant promise as a multi-role naval fighter-bomber, but its reliability must be further confirmed in future test flights.

Next Steps:

Engine modifications to address cold-start issues.

Further testing on low-altitude bombing and maneuvering under full combat conditions.

Pilot training on emergency procedures in case of engine failure.

[b]This report will be sent to the Sikirskian Ministry of Defence and SDF Engineering Division for immediate review.[/b]

> VID_1203.mp4
